tickets.subject: Guest Claim of Bed Bug Bites / Request for Financial Compensation
tickets.description:
Hi Team,

Today, we received an email from VRBO Customer Support regarding a complaint submitted by the guest, Thomas Laube, following his recent stay at Signal Inn - Unit 14.

According to VRBO, the guest reported being bitten by bed bugs while staying at the property. The guest also provided photographic evidence of the alleged bites and is requesting financial compensation for the distress and inconvenience experienced during the stay.

VRBO Support is requesting that we review the matter and provide the following information:
  1. Our response to the guest's complaint.
  2. Confirmation of whether the property has been inspected or treated for bed bugs.
  3. The level of compensation or partial refund, if any, we are willing to offer to resolve the matter.
VRBO has requested a response within 24 to 48 hours.

Internal Findings / Initial Review

  • No complaint or report of bed bug bites was received from Call Center Team from the guest during their stay.
  • According to the onsite team, they did not receive any report or complaint about bed bugs from the guest during the stay.
PLEASE ASSIST.

tickets.subject: Cather Katie | Res #: 66901 | Unit: Pier Pressure | Cancellation Request
tickets.description:
Guest message: 
The application process for the HOA is intrusive. I don’t mind having background checks conducted on my husband and me ;they are very clean), but when I have to start providing private information on my guests (grandchildren) and provide personal references… well, this crosses the life and is not the property for me.
    
Our response:
Hi! Katie, Thank you for sharing your concerns. I completely understand your hesitation regarding the additional information requested as part of the HOA application process. I'd be happy to have this clarified with Brooke and will ask her to give you a call tomorrow to discuss the requirements and address your concerns further. We appreciate you bringing this to our attention. - Marge
   
Guest response:

Thank you Marge. I would appreciate your team simply canceling this rental. The no candle mandate, topped with the overly complicated and intrusive application is already making this unappealing. I have rented homes & condos through VRBO for many years, as well as renting out several of my own properties through this portal. I have never seen such strict rules before. It’s already set the tone for my vacation… I’ll be on pins and needles worrying about following the owners rules versus relaxing (in a responsible manner) and enjoying the stay.

tickets.subject: COLONY INN PRE-ARRIVAL MESSAGE
tickets.description:
Hi Beth,

tickets.subject: VR Compensation Tracker
tickets.description:
Hi

I'd like to request your help building a company-wide system for tracking guest compensations (refunds, credits, free nights, gift cards, goodwill gestures). I've attached as a reference an excel sheet with a wishlist of parameters and info for the fields and reporting we need. It works for one person or team, but it can't give us the access controls, approval workflow, or audit trail we need as we to truly roll this out in a manner that would marry ops decisions to info needed by accounting

GOAL
A single, shared system where staff with authority to give compensation company wide can submit compensation requests, approvals route automatically based on the dollar amount, each resort's data stays separate from the others, and Accounting can audit and reconcile everything in one place.

REQUIREMENTS

1. Submission
- A simple form or entry screen that any authorized staff member can use, on desktop or mobile.
- Fields should match the attached tracker: date logged, guest name, reservation #, resort/property, booking platform, check-in/check-out, issue category, description, compensation type, amount, date compensation was given, booking total, cost borne by (Company, Owner, Vendor, Platform, Insurance), work order for owner charges and notes.
- Dropdowns for the standard lists, managed by an admin rather than typed freely.
- Ability to attach supporting documents (guest messages, photos, invoices).

2. Tiered approval workflow
- Requests route automatically to the right approver based on amount, for example:
  - Tier 1: Amount TBD - Call Center/FOC
  - Tier 2: Amount TBD - Call Center Manager/Resort Manager
  - Tier 3: Amount TBD -  Customer Experience Manager/Regional Mananger
- Thresholds and approvers must be editable by an admin without developer help.
- Email notifications to approvers, with approve / deny / request-more-info actions and a required comment on denials.
- Statuses:  Approved, Issued, Denied.
- Requesters cannot approve their own requests.

3. Resort-level data separation
- Users see and submit only for the resort(s) they are assigned to.
- Resort managers see only their own resort's records.
- Regional or corporate roles can see multiple or all resorts.
- Access is assigned through roles or groups, so staffing changes are easy to manage.

4. Audit and accounting access
- Accounting has read access to all resorts, plus the ability to mark compensations as Issued / Reconciled and record the payment date and reference.
- A full audit trail: who created, edited, approved, or denied each record, with timestamps and the previous values for any changes.
- Approved and issued records are locked from editing, or any change is logged and requires re-approval.
- Records cannot be deleted, only voided with a reason.

5. Reporting
- Dashboards or exportable reports by resort, issue category, compensation type, cost bearer, approver, and month.
- Pending and aging views, including days from request to resolution.
- Export to Excel/CSV for Accounting and owner statements.

NICE TO HAVE
- Integration with our property management system and accounting software, if feasible.
- Automatic flag for repeat compensations to the same guest or repeated issues at the same unit.
- Monthly summary emailed to resort managers and Accounting.

QUESTIONS FOR YOU
1. Which platform do you recommend, and is it covered by our existing licenses?
2. What's a realistic timeline and level of effort?
3. Is there anything you need from me, such as workflow diagrams, approver lists, or user/resort assignments?
4. Who should own the system administration once it's live?

TIMELINE
We'd like to have this live by [target date]. Happy to set up a short call to walk through the attached tracker and answer questions. I can also bring in Accounting and a resort manager to confirm the approval and audit requirements.

Thank you,
Sandra Soria Frausto
Director of Operations

tickets.subject: 3 Star Review Feedback | Res #: 64927 | Chang Christina | Beach House Residences Unit 1 | 11/6/2026 - 11/9/2026
tickets.description:
Hello Jessica,

Hope all is well. I wanted to share with you a 3-star review we received direct from the guest with some feedback. Below you will find the review.

"Overall, our stay was positive. The apartment is spacious and comfortable with the added benefit of two parking spaces given the challenge of street parking nearby. The space had just about everything we needed for our stay - well-stocked kitchen, cleaning supplies, washer/dryer, and linens/towels. The close proximity to the beach as well as a covered balcony and private pool were also big pluses.We did, however, encounter several issues during our stay, and while I received prompt responses, none of the issues were ultimately addressed. The keypad to the garage did not work. The garage door would not open without using the emergency release. The vent fan in the master bathroom did not work and it also dripped brown condensation liquid that stained the toilet seat lid cover and toilet seat. There was a bag of children's clothes and other items in a plastic bag left by the door that we believed may have either been left behind by the previous guest or by the cleaning crew. On the day of check-in, I didn't receive entry code and other access details until I directly reached out at 5pm.In the end, these were minor inconveniences, and other than the time and effort we spent troubleshooting the garage door issue, they did not affect the overall enjoyment of our stay."

1) Garage door keypad did not work

2) The vent fan in the master bathroom did not work and it also dripped brown condensation liquid that stained the toilet seat lid cover and toilet seat

3) There was a bag of children's clothes and other items in a plastic bag left by the door that we believed may have either been left behind by the previous guest or by the cleaning crew

4) They didn't receive entry code and other access details until I directly reached out at 5pm

tickets.subject: Signal Inn Unit 06 Description Update
tickets.description:
Hi David,

I received a message from Lais, The owner of Unit 06 wants us to update the Airbnb Description, For your assistance please 


The space
 
Enjoy relaxed island living in this tropical, beachfront, one-bedroom, one-bath elevated retreat at pet-friendly Signal Inn on Sanibel Island. Unit 6, an ideal couples hide-away, features beach views and sunlight throughout. This ideally situated end unit is accessed by a single flight of stairs allowing for two dedicated parking spots directly below the unit along with expansive beach views over the mangrove forest.
 
The beautifully decorated open living, dining and kitchen space makes entertaining and meal prep a breeze. It features an oversized sliding door leading to a private screened lanai with dining for four and additional seating. This units thoughtfully chosen furniture and lighting with artwork throughout brings the beach experience inside. This inspiring interior will have you primed to explore all that this special spot offers... just beyond the front door. The spacious primary bedroom features a king-size bed, TV and plenty of accessible storage. The adjacent full bathroom includes a modern white tiled walk-in shower with stone flooring and black hardware completing this sophisticated space. 

Some of this units’ features include:
  • Sleeper sofa in living room
  • In-unit washer and dryer
  • A full range of fresh, cotton beach, bath and hand towels
  • Roku and Xfinity cable service with sports channels including Golf Channel and Tennis Channel
  • Fully equipped kitchen 
 
Signal Inn, Sanibel’s premier pet-friendly beachfront community, offers private boardwalk access to your next sunrise or sunset on the best shelling beach in the world. When not beachcombing or relaxing on the shoreline, guests can enjoy the resort’s heated pool, hot tub, pool deck lounges and tables set among palms and tropical landscaping. Charcoal grills, situated throughout the property await fresh catch-of-the-day from Sanibel’s farmer’s market or grocery.

 

With Signal Inn being situated directly on the Sanibel bike network, a short peddle will get you to the grocery store, dining, shopping and local athletic clubs open to the public offering pickleball, tennis and golf. Also nearby are the Sanibel Lighthouse, community fitness center, and the Ding Darling and Tarpon Bay nature preserves. 
 
Additional Details & House Rules
  • Beach Gear & Tech: Beach towels, chairs, and umbrellas are provided, and all TVs feature Roku.
  • Pet Policy: Up to 2 pets are welcome.
  • Rules: No smoking, no burning candles indoors, and no parties.
  • Hospitality and management by Gulf Coast 

 

 

Dwelling License: RDWL-005748

According to the property details, we need to contact the owner for approval before proceeding with any repairs. Would you be able to help us obtain approval for an HVAC inspection?

Thank you.

tickets.subject: Weisberg Suzanne/Sandalfoot 2B1/Res #: 66077/Cancellation Request
tickets.description:
AIRBNB - MODERATE
Reason for Cancelling: Guest father in law passed away today

I have done my best to explain our cancellation policy, including that we are required to follow Airbnb's terms and that, given how close the arrival date is, a full refund is unlikely. I also suggested finding someone who could take over the reservation, but the guest mentioned that they don't know anyone who could use the booking.


The guest then asked whether we could consider exercising host discretion or provide credit toward a future reservation, as they would still like to rebook after the holidays. I explained the business impact of last-minute cancellations and assured her that I would coordinate her request with upper management for further consideration.

I understand that we need to protect the owner's and company's interests, but given the unfortunate circumstances, I'd appreciate your guidance on whether we can consider an exception, partial refund, or future booking credit.

tickets.description:
Hello Lais,

We received this 1 star review with some feedback that I wanted to share with you. Below you will find the review.

""Overall the worst rental we have ever had. My wife and I spent a week here, and we had great weather, a really nice view and enjoyed our week together relaxing. That’s what we tried to focus on, but the facts are that this rental unit is horrid and should not be rented to anyone at any price! The entire unit is run down! A number of the light switches don’t work, the fan on the patio does not work, there is no way to lock the sliding doors to the patio from the living room or the bedroom which means there is access into the unit from the roof down the spiral staircase into the patio. The most important issue is the horrible smell throughout the rental unit which we could not get rid of despite having the property management company place Damp Rids throughout. We also needed to have the property management company cut PVC pipe to secure the sliding glass doors. There were dead bugs in the corner of our bathroom and dead bugs/something growing under the sink all stuck to the dish draining rack. This is easily the worst rental property we have ever had. And in hindsight, we should’ve refused to stay there. After a lot of cajoling, we forced the property management company to give us 25% discount on the unit which in reality was a giant compromise because I would not have accepted a stay for free at this property if I knew what it was like. The property management company knew full well the issues in this unit and had done nothing about it until we forced them to address some of the issues. The only reputable actions we received from the property management company was from Jen, who came over and tried to help us deal with these issues. Hats off to her, but a giant F to the property management company who I would never ever recommend."

4) Horrible smell throughout the rental.

5) There were dead bugs in the corner of our bathroom and dead bugs/something growing under the sink all stuck to the dish draining rack.

Thank you.

tickets.subject: 5 Star Review Feedback | Res #: 62564 | Westin Taylor | Colony Inn C-55 | 10/23/2026 - 10/25/2026
tickets.description:
Hello Marcie,

We received this 5 star review with some feedback from the guest that I wanted to share with you. Below you will find the review.

"
Thank you for sharing such thoughtful feedback about your stay at Colony Inn C-55! We're happy you enjoyed the convenient location on Sanibel Island and were able to take advantage of the beach supplies and shell washing station. Those little conveniences can make a beach vacation even more enjoyable!

We enjoyed our stay, the condo is in a great location, with all beach supplies available to borrow, and a shell washing station which was a nice perk.  

A few things to consider, the set up is odd bedroom right inside the door, so no one can step outside if other people are sleeping, because then everyone will be awake. No basics (ie salt, pepper). Check-in being 4pm and check-out is just too early especially having to start dishwasher and take out all of your trash. Additionally, the lights and a/c were hard to figure out and we couldn’t figure out how to turn down the AC in the living room so we were freezing. A few small throw blankets would have been a nice addition.

Feedback Identified:

1) Air conditioner and lighting controls were difficult to operate. Maybe need better instructions.

2) Provide basic seasonings like salt and pepper.

3) Extra throw blanket available

4) Concerned about the check out time being too early.

41.

Outstanding Owner Balances and Carrying Charges

Owner is responsible for timely payment of all property-related expenses, maintenance charges, fees, and other amounts due under this Agreement.
Any balance remaining unpaid more than thirty (30) days after being posted to the owner's account will be subject to a 1.5% monthly carrying charge, assessed at the end of each month.

Convo Source: POST ARRIVAL CALL 

Date of Their Stay: CI: 11/02/2026 to CO: 11/05/2026


Date of Incident/Complaint: 11.06.2026

Was it a one-time occurrence, or is it a continuous issue? continuous issue

Summary of the Complaint: 
The guest is requesting a review of the compensation offered due to the air conditioning issues experienced during their stay at Unit 1206.

According to the guest, the air conditioning was not functioning properly on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, with indoor temperatures reaching approximately 82°F and later increasing to 84°F. They also mentioned that technicians attempted to resolve the issue on two separate occasions, but the problem persisted.
Additionally, the guest expressed concern that the AC issue may have already existed during the previous week. They also noted that there were no fans available above the upstairs beds, which made the situation even more uncomfortable.
Previous Compensation Offered:
The guest stated that they had previously been offered:

tickets.subject: Teams Background
tickets.description:
David,

I would like you to take the lead on creating standardized, professional background templates for each of our Gulf Coast brands. My goal is to establish a consistent, polished, and recognizable brand image across all divisions.

Currently, we have employees using a variety of backgrounds, including some that have been personally created or belong to the wrong division. This creates inconsistencies in how our company and its brands are represented, particularly during virtual meetings with clients, board members, vendors, and internal teams.

What I Would Like You to Create
Please develop two distinct background options for each of our brands:
  • Gulf Coast Property Management (GCPM) – Corporate
  • Gulf Coast Association Management (GCAM)
  • Gulf Coast Home Services (GCHS)
  • Gulf Coast Vacation Rentals (GCVR)
  • Island Vacations (IVSC)
Each brand should have the following options:
Option 1 – Professional Corporate Background
  • Clean, sophisticated, and professional design.
  • Appropriate brand logo, colors, and visual identity.
  • Minimal distractions, with the logo clearly visible.
  • Suitable for client meetings, board presentations, and everyday business use.
Option 2 – Modern Branded Background
  • A more contemporary and visually appealing design while maintaining a professional appearance.
  • Incorporate the individual brand's colors, logo, and identity.
  • Provide some variety while keeping the overall Gulf Coast family of brands visually consistent.
Design & Branding Expectations
While each division has its own identity, I would like the overall designs to have a cohesive look and feel. Employees should be immediately recognizable as representing their respective Gulf Coast brand.

Please ensure all backgrounds are properly sized and optimized for Microsoft Teams, with logos positioned so they are not obstructed by the person appearing on camera.

Implementation & Timeline
My goal is to have this initiative fully implemented within the next 30 days, preferably sooner.
I would like you to:
  1. Develop two background options for each brand.
  2. Submit the designs to HR for review and approval.
  3. Make any necessary revisions and finalize the approved templates.
  4. Provide HR with the final files, organized by brand, so they can be distributed to employees.
  5. Coordinate with HR, as needed, to ensure employees can easily access and install their appropriate backgrounds.
Moving Forward – Company Standard
Once these templates are approved and distributed, I would like to establish a company-wide standard requiring employees to use only the approved backgrounds for their assigned brand during business-related virtual meetings.

Personally created backgrounds, outdated designs, or backgrounds representing another division should no longer be used unless specifically authorized.

This will help us maintain a consistent, professional image across all of our brands and ensure we are presenting ourselves appropriately to our clients and business partners.

Please let me know your anticipated timeline for providing the initial designs. I would love to get this rolled out as quickly as possible.

tickets.subject: Van den Heerik Jenette | Unit: Turtle House | Res #: 59381 | Guest Feedback
tickets.description:
Convo source: (SL or Guest called) SL guest email

Date of their stay: 10/23/2026 to 10/28/2026

Date of incident/complaint: 10/31/2026

Summary of the complaint:

: We received and SL guest email containing Feedback regarding their previous stay at the property Turtle House. As per guest:

"Dear Gulf Coast Vacation Rentals,

First of all, we would like to say that the house itself was absolutely fantastic. It was a beautiful property with a lovely swimming pool and a wonderful place to stay. We have no complaints about the house itself.
However, we would like to bring a few points to your attention, as we believe they deserve some extra consideration for future guests.
We arrived after a long journey from the Netherlands, including a flight of approximately ten hours. We would have expected at least one roll of toilet paper to be provided. Especially when arriving late after such a long journey, it is only reasonable to expect that there would be toilet paper available.
We were also disappointed that we were asked to pay $50 for checking in just an hour and a half earlier. We paid over $1,000 for our stay and have been renting holiday homes and Airbnb properties for at least ten years. In our experience, when an earlier check-in is possible, it is usually offered as a courtesy without an additional charge. We therefore decided not to take advantage of this option.
There are also a few maintenance issues that we believe really need attention:
  • The sinks in the master bedroom: There is absolutely no hot water coming from the sinks. We eventually had to get hot water from the bathtub instead.
  • The drainage and plumbing: When we emptied the bathtub in the master bedroom, dirty brown water came back up through the shower drain in the other bathroom. As a result, we were unable to use that bathroom. We suspect there may be a problem with the drainage system or plumbing. We strongly recommend having this checked before the next guests arrive.
  • The outdoor shower: Unfortunately, we did not use the outdoor shower. There were cracks and damaged tiles that could easily cause someone to cut their feet. In addition, the outdoor shower was not clean. Since we enjoy going to the beach, this was particularly disappointing.
Finally, we would like to mention something about communication. It would be much more convenient if guests had one dedicated point of contact throughout their stay. Instead, we were repeatedly put in touch with different people, both through the app and over the phone. We did not find this pleasant, and it caused unnecessary confusion. In our experience with other holiday rentals, we have always had one consistent contact person.
Once again, the house itself was truly beautiful, and we certainly enjoyed the property. That is precisely why we feel it is important to share this feedback with you. It would be a shame if future guests were to experience the same problems.
We sincerely hope you will take our feedback seriously and address these points before welcoming your next guests. "

Evidence to support the complaint :

Unit Changes:
  • The guest was moved to Unit 10 for the night of October 29 only.
  • Beginning October 30 through November 3, the guest will stay in Unit 08.
  • No ground-floor unit was available for the entire 5-night stay, so this was the best available accommodation option.

  • I created a separate reservation for Unit 10 for the first night.
  • Per the agreement, the Unit 10 owner will receive their share of the $137.69 rental revenue from the original Airbnb reservation, with GCVR retaining its portion as applicable.
  • I then modified the reservation in Streamline so that the remaining stay is assigned to Unit 08 from October 30 through November 3.
  • This change was made in Streamline only and should not affect the Airbnb reservation.
Could you please verify that both the Unit 10 owner and Unit 08 owner receive the appropriate rental income for their respective portions of the stay?

Thank you for your assistance.

tickets.subject: Fireside Cottage – Verify Lynx Lock and Guest Key Access
tickets.description:
Issue Description:

The owner reported having video footage showing that the guest may have changed the lock and had additional keys made. However, the team confirmed that the Lynx lock is currently online with 93% battery, and the team also mentioned that the Lynx lock was recently changed.

Required Actions:
  1. Verify the current lock installation and confirm whether the lock has been tampered with or replaced.
  2. Coordinate with the owner to review the video footage and clarify what changes were observed.
  3. Confirm whether any unauthorized keys were made and whether the guest still has access to the property.
  4. Verify that the current lock is functioning properly and that authorized access codes remain secure.
  5. Report the findings and recommend any necessary corrective action.
Note: Please coordinate with the owner and Operations before making any changes to the lock or access settings.

Booking details:

  • Booking ID: 65313
  • Property address: 419 East Gulf Drive, Sanibel, FL, USA

To help protect your property, your neighbors, and your account, please take these steps now:

Remind your guests that disruptive or unauthorized events are strictly prohibited.

Vrbo does not allow disruptive or unauthorized events. Please contact the guest for Booking ID 65313 to confirm the purpose of their trip and to remind them of this policy.

What to do after contacting the guest

If you remain uncomfortable about the booking after contacting the guest, you may cancel without penalty and the guest will receive a full refund. If you do not reach out beforehand and a disruptive event occurs, your listing(s) may be suspended.

Prevent issues before they escalate

Establish a line of communication with your neighbors so they can alert you if there’s a disruptive event at "419 East Gulf Drive, Sanibel, FL, USA". If they can’t reach you, we recommend they contact local authorities.

Consider a noise-monitoring device from NoiseAware

You can proactively monitor your property while respecting guests’ privacy by using a noise-monitoring device. Vrbo offers exclusive discounts on devices and subscriptions. Guests must be notified in advance.

Follow local regulations

Many areas prohibit one-night stays or gatherings above a certain number of guests. Failure to follow local laws can put your Vrbo account at risk.

Report disruptive events immediately

If a guest hosts a disruptive or unauthorized event at your property, notify us as soon as possible and reference the Booking ID 65313. If one takes place, you are expected to notify Vrbo immediately and cooperate fully in our investigation. We encourage you to take time to review Vrbo's policy.

Contact us for assistance or to submit a complaint. In emergencies, call local authorities.

tickets.description:
Property/Guest: Ronald - Green View Getaway
Stay Dates: December 01, 2026 – January  31, 2027


Issue Summary:
The guest is concerned about the lack of mailbox access at the property, as mailbox keys are not available. He explained that he needs to be physically present in Florida to rent a USPS PO Box and cannot arrange mail forwarding until he has a receiving address. He is concerned that his mail will accumulate at his current residence while he travels to Florida.

The guest is asking whether he is still within the cancellation period to receive a full refund due to this concern.

Action Taken:
I clarified that we cannot guarantee access to mail delivered to the property and provided the official USPS PO Box website as an alternative.

Request for Property Manager:

Please let us know if the owner would consider an exception regarding mailbox access and what options may be available, so we can provide the guest with an accurate update. Thank you!

tickets.description:
Hello Marcie,

Hope all is well. We received this Airbnb 3 star review with some feedback that I wanted to share with you. Below you will find the review.

"I was traveling solo with my two kids from a wedding 30 mins north in ft myers and decided to spend a night in Sanibel while down there.
The property is managed by a company which means they are not flexible, they shifted check in at time of booking from 3 pm to 4pm which was too late with little kids. We arrived the same time as the maids at 3pm and couldn’t get in earlier. Check out was at 10 am which is ridiculous for such a late check in time - no value on one night stay just go to a hotel for the price.

Unit doesn’t come with any water or filter just two coffee pods. Lots of beach supplies. Bring your own coffee creamer.

Condo is newer and clean. Ghost ants seem to be a problem if you drop any food on the ground. Response time from mgmt group was quick.
Didn’t care for lock it was hard to tell if it was locked but did have a chain which was good since was solo
Beds were comfortable"

Feedback identified:

1) Upset about our check-in and check-out times.

2) Unit doesn’t come with any water or filter just two coffee pods.

3)  Ghost ants seem to be a problem if you drop any food on the ground.
